source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Watermelon insect pests fall into two main groups.

Sap-sucking insects (ពួកជញ្ជក់): aphids, whitefly (មមាច), thrips (មមង), and fruit flies (រុយស).

Leaf- and stem-cutting insects (ពួកកាត់ស្លឹកនិងដើម): armyworm/cutworm types, fruit-boring caterpillars, cutworms that cut the stem, and leaf-rolling caterpillars/leafminers.

Control measures: keep weeds around the base of plants cut and controlled appropriately; select an appropriate planting season; choose pest-resistant, short-duration varieties. Chemical control uses organophosphate insecticides such as Monocrotophos, Azodrin, Diazinon, or Mevinphos, applied about once a week when adult pests are observed; spraying is done in the cool part of the day (evening).
